message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I wouldn’t call this ECG normal.** From the image, I see:

- A fast, very regular rhythm, approximately **150 beats/minute**.
- QRS complexes that appear widened, suggesting abnormal electrical conduction.
- ST-segment and T-wave changes that need clinical interpretation.

The exact rhythm and cause can’t be confirmed from this image alone. Widened complexes can occur with a bundle branch block or certain abnormal fast rhythms. [Merck Manual](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/cardiovascular-tests-and-procedures/electrocardiography)

**If this is your current ECG and you have chest pain, shortness of breath, marked dizziness, or fainting, call your local emergency number now; don’t drive yourself.** These symptoms with a fast heartbeat warrant emergency care. [NHS guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/heart-palpitations/)

If you feel well but this was just recorded at rest, arrange urgent assessment today, especially if the fast pulse persists.

Are you having symptoms now, and was this taken at rest or after exercise?
